combinations.name: MAOIs
combinations.description: Phenelzine, tranylcypromine, selegiline, etc. — MAO inhibition leaves the catecholamine surge nowhere to go, so pressor effects stack into hypertensive crisis. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Alcohol
combinations.description: The liver combines the two into **cocaethylene** — a second active stimulant with a longer half-life and more cardiac strain than cocaine itself. The pairing feels smoother, which is exactly why both tend to get redosed further than either alone.

combinations.name: Beta-blockers
combinations.description: Not the danger it is rumored to be. The 'unopposed alpha-stimulation' warning came from case reports; outcome data show no excess harm from beta-blockade in cocaine-positive patients. The narrow remaining concern is non-selective propranolol during active cocaine chest pain — outside that, being on a beta-blocker is not itself a red flag.
